excerpt: An ANOVA on overall RT and accuracy collapsed across conditions showed a significant main effect of time [F(1,16) = 13.6, p < .001], with RTs faster at Time 2 than at Time 1, but no significant group interaction. The discussion adds that conflict monitoring differences were absent at Time 2 and that the study should be interpreted cautiously because training groups were small and future studies need active controls and neural measurements.
overview: This evidence captures the main constraint on the paper's interpretation. Practice or task-exposure effects can improve performance over repeated ANT sessions, especially for conflict monitoring, which may obscure group-specific training effects. The limitations also caution against treating the behavioral findings as a complete mechanism without active-control, neural, and more tightly standardized intervention designs.
title: Task Repetition Limits
